title: Trenton charter amendment petition to bar data centers above 25 MW is ordered onto a ballot; election date unresolved

facts.court_decision: 2026-Ohio-3406 (State ex rel. Blankenship v. Trenton City Council, No. 2026-1035)
facts.election_date_per_court: special election 60-120 days after certification; November 3 ballot NOT required

summary: The Ohio Supreme Court ordered Trenton City Council to certify a citizen charter amendment that would prohibit data centers above 25 MW. The court said the city must hold a special election 60 to 120 days after certification and was not required to place the measure on the November general-election ballot. Press reports describe the measure as headed to the Nov. 3 ballot, so the election date needs confirmation.
source_title: Journal-News — Trenton data center charter amendment (Sept. 1, 2026 report)
verbatim: The amendment would prohibit the construction of data centers requiring more than 25 megawatts within city limits.
notes: Court text verified on courtnewsohio.gov (fetched): 'the constitution requires the city to call a special election between 60 and 120 days after passage of an ordinance' and 'the city is not required to submit the proposed amendment for inclusion on this year's general election ballot.' This CONFLICTS with the brief and sites.json (Nov 3). WCPO and Fox19 (fetched) say 'The issue is headed to voters Nov. 3'; the Journal-News 25 MW sentence was fetched verbatim. The word 'Issue 17' and the 'aggregate monthly demand or peak load' wording appear only in search summaries and a Fox19 fetch summary, not in the measure text. The Butler County BOE ballot-issue list and the charter text were NOT reachable (elections.bcohio.gov fetch shows only the Nov 3, 2026 general election header dated July 14). Ohio Supreme Court decision date 2026-09-01. Do not record Nov 3 as the election date until the BOE certifies the measure.

title: Mount Pleasant Plan Commission approves amended Microsoft Durand Avenue site plan, cutting buildings from nine to seven

facts.village_board_vote: expected later in October 2026 (not yet taken)

summary: The Mount Pleasant Plan Commission unanimously approved Microsoft's amended site plan for the Durand Avenue parcel on Oct. 14, reducing the campus from nine to seven data center buildings. A Microsoft spokesperson said the changes do not reflect a reduction in ambition. The Village Board is expected to vote later in October.
source_title: Wisconsin Public Radio — Microsoft fewer data centers sprawling Mount Pleasant campus
verbatim: On Wednesday, the Mount Pleasant Plan Commission unanimously approved the amended site plan.
notes: WPR article dated Oct. 15, 2026 (fetched). 'On Wednesday' = Oct. 14, 2026, consistent with the WPR photo caption 'The Mount Pleasant Plan Commission meets on Oct. 14, 2026.'
